\title{A Guardrailed 23.5\%-Efficient CsPbI3 Constrained Maximum by Multi-Parameter SCAPS-1D Screening: Interface Dose--Response, Sensitivity, and a Reproducibility Audit}
\author{Hussain Touhid Siddiquee\thanks{Department of EEE, Leading University, Sylhet-3112, Bangladesh. E-mail: touhidsiddiqueeraj@gmail.com, mdabdulmalekfahim@gmail.com.} \and Md.\ Abdul Malek Fahim}

\noindent{\small\textit{\textbf{Abstract:} We map how far a SCAPS-1D model of an ITO/TiO2/CsPbI3/CBTS/Ni cell can go inside a stated parameter box --- and what the same model says at realistic settings. A five-factor grid screen (96 runs) plus refinement (36 runs; 126 converged) reaches 23.49\% (Voc 1.234 V, Jsc 21.19 mA/cm$^2$, FF 89.78\%) at 2.2~$\mu$m, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ (single-crystal grade), $R_s=0$, and $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ interface defects: the best point in the stated box, not a fab-ready recipe. At routine $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ a dedicated thickness sweep peaks at 20.82\% (1.0~$\mu$m), and a combined realistic case (ITO 4.4~eV, $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ interfaces) gives 20.68\%. A measured interface dose--response on our own cell runs 25.04\% at $10^8$~cm$^{-2}$ down to 20.64\% at $10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$; the published 24.17\% and 24.24\% values fall below our no-interface band (24.73--25.16\%), and we do not map other groups' stacks onto our curve. Scripted parasitic sweeps give 23.07\% at $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$ and 23.38\% at $R_{sh}=10^4~\Omega$cm$^2$. A Morris sensitivity screen ($r=8$, $p=4$, 56 runs) ranks interface quality first (1.02 points/decade), ahead of bulk defects (0.68) and bandgap. Measured band offsets (absorber CB 0.07~eV above ETL CB: downhill extraction; absorber VB 0.08~eV below HTL VB: shallow favourable offset) and contact work-function tests bound the remaining assumptions. All definition files, sweep receipts, and raw curves are archived for independent reproduction.}}

\medskip
\noindent{\small\textbf{Keywords:} CsPbI3; perovskite solar cell; SCAPS-1D; CBTS; reproducibility; device simulation}

\section{Introduction}

All-inorganic CsPbI3 perovskite solar cells combine the thermal stability lacking in hybrid organic--inorganic perovskites with a bandgap near 1.7~eV that suits both single-junction and tandem top-cell applications~\cite{Dai2026,Qiu2025}. After years below 19\%, certified laboratory efficiencies have recently passed 22\%: 22.02\% certified (22.60\% laboratory) with a moisture-responsive propyltriethoxysilane crystallisation strategy~\cite{Dai2026}, 22.05\% by fluorination-assisted interfacial dipole engineering~\cite{Qiu2025}, 21.71\% with dual-interface and bulk co-passivation at an open-circuit voltage of 1.27~V~\cite{Zhang2026}, and 21.43\% certified for inverted architectures~\cite{Joule2026}. Each record was won at the interfaces and in the bulk defect chemistry, which motivates a simulation study that treats those exact levers honestly.

The one-dimensional solar cell capacitance simulator (SCAPS-1D) is the workhorse for such pre-experimental screening, and the ITO/TiO2/CsPbI3/CBTS (copper barium thiostannate) stack of \citet{Hossain2023} is the most-prescribed CsPbI3 baseline, progressing from 17.90\% over 96 screened transport-layer combinations~\cite{Hossain2022} to 19.06\% after optimisation. Subsequent simulation studies report up to 24.17\% on the same stack~\cite{Nazli2025} and 24.24\% on ZnO/PTAA~\cite{Oyedele2023}, while large machine-learning-coupled screens now exceed 27\% on other absorbers~\cite{PerovskiteOpt2026,Bifacial2026}. Three problems accompany this inflation. First, nearly every study optimises one variable at a time (OVAT), so parameter interactions---notably absorber thickness versus defect-limited diffusion length---are invisible by construction. Second, the highest numbers are obtained with interface recombination removed (stated explicitly in~\cite{Oyedele2023}) or with defect densities far below experimental reach, and raw data are routinely withheld~\cite{Hossain2023}. Third, scripted sweeps mix unit systems: SCAPS definition files store SI units while script `set' commands expect practical units, so SI-valued inputs silently inject a $10^6\times$ overdose and fabricate ghost cells (scripting conventions are documented in Appendix~A).

This work contributes (i) a five-factor grid screen (96 configurations) plus refinement (36 runs) of the ITO/TiO2/CsPbI3/CBTS/Ni cell under interface-inclusive guardrails, reaching \textbf{23.49\%} as the best point in the stated box; (ii) a measured interface dose--response on our own cell running 25.04\% to 20.64\% as interface quality degrades; (iii) scripted (not analytic) series- and shunt-resistance accounting; and (iv) a Morris sensitivity screen that ranks interface quality above all bulk factors. Every definition file, sweep receipt, and raw curve is archived for independent reproduction.


\section{Literature: a decade of CsPbI3 progress}

Black-phase CsPbI3 has been stabilised stepwise since 2016: quantum-dot-induced $\alpha$-phase retention at 10.8\%~\cite{Swarnkar2016}, co-evaporated planar cells at 17.0\%~\cite{Frolova2017}, thermodynamically stable $\gamma$-films~\cite{Zhao2018}, surface-passivated 14.5\% devices~\cite{Bian2018}, and compositionally engineered 13--14\% cells~\cite{Xi2019,Becker2019}, all on TiO2 with Spiro-OMeTAD, PTAA or carbon contacts~\cite{Luo2016,Ke2018,Xiang2018}. The 2019 aziridinium result at 18.40\%~\cite{Wang2019} stood for years until the 2025--2026 interface-engineering wave (Figure~\ref{fig:timeline}): fluorinated dipoles (22.05\%~\cite{Qiu2025}), dual-interface plus bulk co-passivation with Voc 1.27~V (21.71\%~\cite{Zhang2026}), moisture-responsive crystallisation (22.60\% laboratory, 22.02\% certified~\cite{Dai2026}), and stitched grain-boundary grooves in inverted cells (21.43\% certified~\cite{Joule2026}). The certified frontier is therefore 22.02\%, and every recent jump came from defect and interface control---the precise levers a simulation study must treat honestly.

Simulation studies trace a parallel inflation curve (Table~\ref{tab:lit}). The CBTS screening programme reached 17.90\% over 96 transport-layer combinations~\cite{Hossain2022} and 19.06\% after full optimisation~\cite{Hossain2023}, the baseline we reproduce. Later claims diverge upward as realism constraints are relaxed: 23.10\% with ZnO/Spiro in one report~\cite{Ristiansyah2026}, 24.17\% on our exact stack~\cite{Nazli2025}, and 24.24\% on ZnO/PTAA without interface layers (stated)~\cite{Oyedele2023}. The broader SCAPS literature shows the same pattern across absorbers---MAPbI3 at 19.30\% with inorganic contacts~\cite{Son2024}, gradient-doped FAPbI3 at 20.34\%~\cite{Ritu2024}, a 28.38\% bifacial triple-cation cell~\cite{Bifacial2026}, and an explicitly idealised 40.17\% MASnI3 result that exceeds the Shockley--Queisser bound~\cite{MASnI3ML2026,SQ1961}. Our audit in Section~7.0 places these numbers on a common guardrailed footing.

\section{Simulation framework and guardrails}

Devices were simulated in SCAPS-1D v3.3.10 under AM1.5G illumination (100~mW/cm$^2$) at 300~K unless stated. The baseline reproduces \citet{Hossain2023}: ITO front contact (4.0~eV), 30~nm TiO2 electron transport layer (donor density $9\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$), CsPbI3 absorber (800~nm initial, $E_g=1.694$~eV, $\chi=3.95$~eV, $N_A=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$), 100~nm CBTS hole transport layer ($N_A=10^{18}$~cm$^{-3}$), and Ni back contact (5.5~eV). Crucially, neutral interface recombination blocks ($N=10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$, $\sigma=10^{-19}$~m$^2$) are present at both heterojunctions, and the absorber uses the coefficients-A-and-B absorption model ($A=10^7$~m$^{-1}$eV$^{-1/2}$) so that bandgap sweeps act on the absorption edge rather than a frozen file spectrum. Our unmodified baseline yields 18.99\% (Voc 1.122~V, Jsc 19.68~mA/cm$^2$, FF 86.00\%), reproducing the published 17.9--19.06\% band and validating the harness.

Guardrails enforced throughout: bulk defect floor $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ (single-crystal grade; nothing lower), absorber doping ceiling $3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, conduction-band offset 0 to +0.3~eV maintained by linking $\chi$ to $E_g$ ($\chi=3.95+0.5(E_g-1.694)$), and automatic rejection of runs with Voc above $E_g/q-0.28$~V ($\sim$1.37~V at 1.65~eV, the detailed-balance neighbourhood; the model sets $k_{rad}=0$, so this is a plausibility ceiling, not a computed radiative limit) or FF above Green's ideal-diode value at the measured Voc (90.0\% at 300~K, 90.9\% at 275~K) as non-physical. Series and shunt resistances are scriptable in SCAPS~3.3.10 (\texttt{set external.Rs/Rsh}; \texttt{scriptdescription3310.txt}), so this section reports measured parasitic sweeps. Sweeps ran in parallel on four workers with checkpointed receipts; of 132 grid configurations, 126 converged and enter the analysis (6 non-converged worker runs excluded and listed in the receipts). A duplicate champion run reproduces the coarse-grid value 23.5041\% exactly, confirming determinism; a confirmatory run at finer IV step gives 23.4874\% (FF 89.78\%), reported as 23.49\% throughout. Absorber densities of states are capped at $N_c=1.1\times10^{19}$/$N_v=8.2\times10^{19}$~cm$^{-3}$, ten times below the Table-1 print ($10^{20}$~cm$^{-3}$, above solid density and hence unphysical).


SCAPS-1D solves the Poisson equation coupled to electron and hole continuity with drift-diffusion transport~\cite{Khattak2019,BurgelmanSCAPS}:
\begin{equation}
-\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\varepsilon(x)\frac{\partial V}{\partial x}\right) = q[p-n+N_D^+-N_A^-+p_t-n_t],
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\frac{\partial n}{\partial t}=\frac{1}{q}\frac{\partial J_n}{\partial x}+G_n-R_n,\quad
\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}=-\frac{1}{q}\frac{\partial J_p}{\partial x}+G_p-R_p,
\end{equation}
with Shockley--Read--Hall recombination through the specified bulk and interface defect levels. Optical generation uses the Eg-sqrt (Tauc) model $\alpha=A\sqrt{h\nu-E_g}$, so bandgap sweeps move the absorption edge self-consistently. Full input parameters are listed in Tables~\ref{tab:in} and~\ref{tab:if}; transport-layer screenings that motivate the TiO2/CBTS choice are reviewed in~\cite{Hossain2022,Raoui2019}.

\section{Grid screen and champion best point}

Round~A explored the full cross-product of absorber thickness (1.0--2.0~$\mu$m), acceptor density ($10^{15}$--$10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$), bulk defect density ($10^{12}$--$10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$), ETL donor density ($9\times10^{16}$--$9\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$), and bandgap (1.694/1.65~eV with linked affinity)---96 configurations in a single parallel batch, rather than sequential OVAT slices. The winner (2.0~$\mu$m, $N_A=10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_{D,ETL}=9\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$, $E_g=1.65$~eV) reached 23.47\%. Full parameters are collected in Table~\ref{tab:champ}. Round~B refined thickness (1.8--2.2~$\mu$m), gap (1.65--1.72~eV), and doping around this point (36 configurations) and reached \textbf{23.49\%} (2.2~$\mu$m, $N_A=3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, $E_g=1.65$~eV, $\chi=3.928$~eV): Voc 1.234~V, Jsc 21.19~mA/cm$^2$, FF 89.78\% (Figure~\ref{fig:jvboth}). Two facts about this optimum must be stated plainly. First, it sits at the corner of the allowed box: $N_A$ at its ceiling, $N_t$ at its floor, $N_{D,ETL}$ at the top of its tested range, $E_g$ at its bottom, thickness at the top of the refined range. Second, the best grid point at the literature gap $E_g=1.694$~eV reaches only 22.51\%, so roughly one point of the 23.49\% comes from the gap choice alone. Every top-ten configuration carries $E_g=1.65$~eV, gaining $\sim$1.5~mA/cm$^2$ over 1.694~eV while the $\chi$ link holds the absorber CB 0.07~eV above the ETL CB (downhill extraction); the HTL side carries a shallow 0.08~eV hole-favourable offset outside the ideal window (Section~5.0).

The interaction map (Figure~\ref{fig:contour}) shows why OVAT misses the optimum: thick absorbers (2.0--2.2~$\mu$m) win only jointly with $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, where the diffusion length still covers the thickness, while at $10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$ the optimum collapses below 1.5~$\mu$m. ETL donor density confirms the literature optimum ($9\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$) and transport-layer thicknesses are insensitive (100/30~nm retained), both consistent with~\cite{Hossain2023}. The current--voltage curve (Figure~\ref{fig:jvboth}) is square and artefact-free, with a Voc deficit of 0.42~V against $E_g/q$---typical of realistic rather than idealised cells.

The 4.50-point stacked gain decomposes along the screening path (Table~\ref{tab:champ} parameters in sequence, illustrative ordering only): thickness 800~nm to 1.5~$\mu$m adds 0.19 points (19.18\%), acceptor doping to $10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ adds 0.93 points (20.11\%), bulk-defect reduction to $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ adds $\sim$1.6 points ($\sim$21.7\%), and the joint $E_g$--$\chi$ move to 1.65~eV with ETL donor optimisation contributes the remaining $\sim$1.8 points. This sequential attribution is order-dependent and illustrative, not causal. Open-circuit voltage climbs 1.122 to 1.234~V while the fill factor rises 86.0 to 89.8\%, the signature of SRH-lifetime recovery rather than band-shift artefacts.

Round~A's top ten (Table~\ref{tab:top10}) all carry $E_g=1.65$~eV; the top seven sit at $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ while rows 8--10 at $N_t=10^{13}$~cm$^{-3}$ trail by $\sim$0.4 points through Voc loss (1.233 to 1.221~V). Round~B refined thickness (1.8--2.2~$\mu$m), gap (1.65--1.72~eV) and doping (36 runs) and moved the best from 23.47\% to 23.50\% (coarse grid), i.e.\ the landscape is converged rather than climbing.

Round~B's refinement is documented in full because its plateau is itself evidence: the best ten span only 23.32--23.50\% (Table~\ref{tab:top10b}), with thickness 1.8--2.2~$\mu$m and $N_A$ (1--3)$\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ numerically indistinguishable at grid resolution once $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ and $E_g=1.65$~eV are fixed (the ten span 23.32--23.50\%, a 0.18-point range against a 0.017-point coarse/fine IV-step uncertainty, so the leading cluster cannot be separated even though the 10th entry trails observably). The $N_t=3\times10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ entries trail by $\sim$0.05 points, confirming the defect floor binds the optimum.

\section{Band alignment}

Figure~\ref{fig:align} constructs the equilibrium alignment from the champion parameters. The absorber conduction edge ($-3.928$~eV) lies 0.07~eV \textit{above} the TiO2 edge ($-4.00$~eV), so electrons move downhill into the ETL: a 0.07~eV cliff, not a spike, with no extraction barrier but a lowered interface recombination activation energy. On the hole side, the absorber valence edge ($-5.578$~eV) lies 0.08~eV \textit{below} the CBTS edge ($-5.50$~eV), i.e.\ a shallow hole-favourable offset on the wrong side of the ideal $-0.3$ to $-0.1$~eV window ($-3.928$ vs $-4.00$; $-5.578$ vs $-5.50$). A $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}$ sweep at the champion confirms the picture: 3.4~eV gives 20.22\%, 3.5~eV 22.07\%, 3.7~eV 23.77\%, 3.8~eV 23.81\%, monotonic in the offset exactly as the downhill/uphill reading predicts. The literature 3.6~eV value is therefore not optimal, and the 23.49\% stands inside the stated box rather than at any physical alignment limit.

\section{Device characterisation}

The quantum efficiency (Figure~\ref{fig:qe}) is flat at $\sim$89--90\% from 300~nm with the absorption edge red-shifted from 731~nm (baseline, 1.694~eV) to 752~nm (champion, 1.65~eV), directly explaining the Jsc gain. The UV plateau assumes the definition file's flat 10\% front reflection with no dispersive parasitic absorption in ITO or TiO2, so it is an upper envelope in the blue rather than a prediction. Capacitance--voltage analysis at 1~MHz (Figure~\ref{fig:cv}) shows rising capacitance with forward bias (31 to 39~nF/cm$^2$ over 0--0.5~V; SCAPS-extracted width 0.29 to 0.22~$\mu$m, far below the 2.2~$\mu$m absorber throughout). The forward-bias sweep admits no valid Mott--Schottky extraction---$1/C^2$ falls with voltage, and a na\"ive slope gives an unphysical doping---so no carrier density is inferred and the curve is reported as qualitative consistency only. (The parallel-plate check $\varepsilon A/C$ gives 0.17~$\mu$m at 0~V versus the solver's 0.29~$\mu$m, a further reason not to over-read the electrostatics.) The illuminated band diagram at short circuit (Figure~\ref{fig:eb}) exhibits clean quasi-Fermi splitting, and generation exceeds recombination by at least two orders of magnitude at every mesh point of the full 2.33~$\mu$m short-circuit profile (minimum ratio $\sim$3$\times10^2$ at $x\approx0.2$~$\mu$m near the back contact, rising above $10^5$ at both contacts; Figure~\ref{fig:gr}). All profile statements in this section are at short circuit; nothing here constrains the maximum-power or open-circuit regime.

Temperature dependence (Figure~\ref{fig:t}, Table~\ref{tab:temp}) follows the established trend~\cite{Hossain2023}: efficiency falls from 24.44\% at 275~K to 16.70\% at 475~K, driven by Voc (1.271 to 0.955~V) and FF while Jsc stays pinned at $\sim$21.19~mA/cm$^2$, i.e.\ $-0.16$\%/K relative ($-0.039$ points/K) over 300--400~K. The 275~K fill factor (90.75\%) sits \textit{below} Green's ideal-diode value at that Voc and temperature (90.86\%), so no artefact needs invoking; likewise the champion's 89.78\% is within 0.2 points of ideal (90.0\%), leaving essentially no FF headroom beyond series resistance. The 475~K end of the sweep ignores the temperature dependence of $E_g$ and black-phase stability, so it is a solver stress test, not a prediction.

\subsection{Parasitic-resistance accounting}

Series and shunt resistances are scriptable in SCAPS~3.3.10 (\texttt{set external.Rs/Rsh}; \texttt{scriptdescription3310.txt}). Measured scripted sweeps on the champion give 23.29\% at $R_s=0.5~\Omega$cm$^2$, \textbf{23.07\%} at $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$, and 22.64\% at $R_s=2~\Omega$cm$^2$ (Table~\ref{tab:rs}), agreeing with the analytic derate to 0.02 points. Shunt paths cost 0.11 points at $R_{sh}=10^4~\Omega$cm$^2$ (23.38\%) and 1.27 points at $R_{sh}=10^3~\Omega$cm$^2$ (22.22\%); combined $R_s=1$/$R_{sh}=10^4$ gives 22.95\%. The best point therefore survives realistic parasitics, but only just: at $R_s=2~\Omega$cm$^2$ the margin over the 22.02\% certified record is 0.6 points.

\section{Reproducibility audit: what the 24\%+ claims are made of}

Deleting the interface blocks inflates efficiency by 1.26--1.67 points absolute: 23.40 to 24.87\%, 23.47 to 24.73\%, and 23.50\% coarse (23.49\% fine) to 25.16\% (Figure~\ref{fig:audit}), almost entirely through a $\sim$0.13~V Voc rise as interface recombination vanishes. But the binary ON/OFF comparison understates the audit: the full dose--response (Table~\ref{tab:ifdose}) runs 25.04\% at $10^8$~cm$^{-2}$, 24.54\% at $10^9$~cm$^{-2}$, 23.49\% at the $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ guardrail, 22.88\% at $3\times10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$, 22.21\% at $10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$, and 20.64\% at $10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$. The published 24.17\%~\cite{Nazli2025} and 24.24\%~\cite{Oyedele2023} values fall \textit{below} our no-interface band (24.73--25.16\%). Because their stacks, gaps, thicknesses and defect parameters all differ from ours, we do not map their numbers onto our curve; the dose--response is reported strictly as an own-cell result. We could not re-run either study from its published parameters (neither paper prints a complete parameter table), and we state this as a limitation rather than a finding. Under interface-inclusive settings, the highest reported CsPbI3 value in our survey remains 23.10\% on ZnO/Spiro~\cite{Ristiansyah2026}; our 23.49\% is the best point in the stated box on the TiO2/CBTS stack, and Section~9.0 itemises what could still deflate it.

\subsection{Where the missing points go}

The inflation is almost entirely a Voc effect ($+$0.13~V) with Jsc unchanged to within 0.02~mA/cm$^2$: removing the $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ interface states eliminates the dominant SRH channel at the heterojunctions, unpinning the quasi-Fermi splitting toward the detailed-balance neighbourhood---indeed the no-interface Voc values (1.363--1.382~V) approach the $\sim$1.37~V $E_g$-implied ceiling for 1.65~eV (the model sets $k_{rad}=0$, so closeness to that ceiling marks the edge of the physical regime, not radiative-limited operation). Fill factor moves non-monotonically (89.8 to 87.0\% on the champion) as the recombination profile reshapes. The no-interface 87.0\% at Voc 1.364~V sits 3.7 points below Green's ideal (90.7\%): the archived JV curve stays flat to 1.16~V with no kink or S-shape, so there is no visible extraction barrier, but the knee remains SRH-rounded by the surviving bulk channel---removing interfaces unpins Voc without idealising the diode. This bounds the ``no extraction barriers'' claim to current collection, not to fill factor. Asymmetric tests show both heterojunctions matter: $10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$ on the ETL side alone gives 21.35\%, on the HTL side alone 21.20\%. Raising the capture cross-section $10\times$ at fixed $N_{if}=10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ gives 22.21\%, exactly reproducing the $N\times10$ row, as expected for rate $\propto N\sigma$ with symmetric $\sigma_n=\sigma_p$. (A first attempt via \texttt{set ...capture\_cross\_section} instead silently neutralised one interface block, yielding 23.86\%; that point is discarded and the verified definition-file variant reported. Bulk $N_t\times\sigma$ interacts: $\sigma\times10$ costs 0.23 points at the $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ floor but 1.5 points at routine $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ (17.44\%), while $\sigma\times0.1$ at the floor gains only 0.04 points (23.53\%)---the floor is saturated.) The measured parasitic sweep applied to the guarded champion is tabulated below.

\section{Morris sensitivity screening}

Grid methods with uneven ranges cannot rank physical importance, so we ran a Morris sensitivity screen instead: $r=8$ trajectories, $p=4$ levels, $k=6$ factors (absorber thickness, $\log N_A$, $\log N_t$, $\log N_{D,ETL}$, $E_g$ with the $\chi$ link applied deterministically, and $\log N_{if}$ tied on both interfaces), 56 fresh simulations, all converged, spanning 15.6--23.4\% (Table~\ref{tab:morris}, Figure~\ref{fig:morris}). In physical units, interface quality leads at 1.02 points/decade, ahead of bulk defect density (0.68/decade); bandgap moves 17.5 points/eV, thickness 0.72 points/$\mu$m, and the dopings trail (0.32 and 0.23/decade). The large $\sigma$ values throughout confirm strong interactions/nonlinearity---notably thickness acting through defect-limited diffusion length---so these are screening ranks, not variance shares, and the range choices are printed in the table so the ranking can be re-weighted. Two disclosures: $E_g$ moves together with $\chi$ by construction, and the two interfaces move together, so their scores bundle linked effects.

Interface-led sensitivity is consistent with passivation studies in which interface-adjacent defects gate the voltage~\cite{Li2018}, and with Bayesian optimisation on CsSnI3 where the optimal thickness likewise shifts with defect density~\cite{PerovskiteOpt2026}.







\section{Discussion}

Fabrication plausibility bounds the result, and new sensitivity runs tighten the bounds. $N_A=3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ is routinely achievable; $E_g=1.65$~eV sits below the $\sim$1.7~eV of the experimental records and contributes roughly one point (best 1.694~eV grid point: 22.51\%); $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ demands near-single-crystal quality, and raising the capture cross-section $10\times$ costs a further 0.23 points there and 1.5 points at routine $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$. The contacts are not neutral choices: lowering Ni from 5.5 to 5.0~eV (the usual metal range) costs 0.23 points, and raising ITO from 4.0 to 4.7~eV collapses the cell to 18.60\% (Voc 1.08~V), so the front contact must stay near 4.0--4.4~eV. A $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}$ sweep (3.4 to 3.8~eV) moves efficiency monotonically from 20.22\% to 23.81\%, confirming the corrected alignment reading of Section~5.0 and showing the literature 3.6~eV value is not optimal---the box could be widened, but we keep the surveyed value and report the sensitivity instead. The honest headline at realistic settings is the combined case: ITO 4.4~eV, $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ interfaces gives \textbf{20.68\%}, and the routine-defect thickness sweep peaks at 20.82\% (1.0~$\mu$m). Against experiment: 23.49\% exceeds the 22.02\% certified record by 1.47 points and the 22.60\% laboratory value by 0.89 points; with measured $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$ (23.07\%) the margin over certified is 1.05 points and over laboratory 0.47 points. The result sits at $\sim$78\% of the $\sim$30\% Shockley--Queisser limit at 1.65~eV ($\sim$1.45~V), well inside thermodynamics.


\section{Outlook}

A laboratory translation would need, simultaneously: $\sim$1.0~$\mu$m CsPbI3 films at routine defect levels for the 20.68\% realistic case (time-resolved photoluminescence verified), interface passivation toward $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ following the fluorinated-dipole~\cite{Qiu2025} or dual-interface~\cite{Zhang2026} chemistries, a front contact near 4.0--4.4~eV, and $R_s\le1~\Omega$cm$^2$ (Table~\ref{tab:rs}). We state plainly what is not demonstrated: 2.2~$\mu$m device-quality CsPbI3 at $N_t\sim10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, and sputtered CBTS directly on CsPbI3 (CBTS typically requires high-temperature sulfurisation), for which we found no precedent---so this section is a requirements list, not a recipe. In-line controls, where applicable: QE edge at 752~nm (Figure~\ref{fig:qe}) and the $-0.16$\%/K temperature coefficient (Table~\ref{tab:temp}).


\section{Limitations and outlook}

Five boundaries delimit this work. First, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ at 2.2~$\mu$m demands near-single-crystal films, and with the modelled $\sigma=10^{-19}$~m$^2$ implies $\tau_{\mathrm{SRH}}\approx100$~$\mu$s, one to two orders beyond the best reported perovskite films; at routine $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ a dedicated sweep peaks at 20.82\% (1.0~$\mu$m) and the combined realistic case gives 20.68\%. Second, the contacts (Ni 5.5~eV, ITO 4.0~eV) and the shallow off-window hole-side offset (+0.08~eV) are stated-box choices, each priced in Section~9.0. Third, phase stability of black CsPbI3 against the yellow $\delta$-phase, ion migration, $E_g(T)$, and damp-heat degradation are outside SCAPS-1D steady-state scope and must be validated experimentally, following the passivation routes of~\cite{Qiu2025,Zhang2026,Dai2026}. Fourth, the grid is a screen, not an optimiser: the best point sits at the corner of the allowed box and the leading cluster is numerically inseparable. Fifth, the single-junction ceiling ($\sim$30\% at 1.65~eV~\cite{SQ1961}) caps how far any interface-inclusive screening can go.

\section{Conclusion}

Grid screening under interface-inclusive guardrails finds a 23.49\%-efficient best point in the stated CsPbI3/CBTS box, with every load-bearing assumption priced: single-crystal-grade defects, a low gap, standard-surveyed but tuned contacts, and a shallow off-window hole-side offset. The same campaign prices the realistic-defect result at 20.68\%, measures the interface dose--response on its own cell, replaces an analytic resistance derate with scripted parasitic sweeps, and ranks interfaces first by Morris screening. We recommend guardrailed reporting (interface status \textit{with} dose level, defect floors \textit{with} cross-sections, unit-system declaration, Rs basis, contact work functions) as a publication standard for SCAPS studies.

\section*{Appendix A: the scripting unit trap}

SCAPS definition files store SI units (metres, m$^{-3}$, m$^2$/Vs) but script \texttt{set} commands expect practical units ($\mu$m, cm$^{-3}$, cm$^2$/Vs)---verified by dose--response: \texttt{set layer2.NA 1e15} reproduces the file baseline (stored $10^{21}$~m$^{-3}$) exactly, while SI-valued inputs (e.g. $10^{22}$) inject a $10^6\times$ overdose and yield degenerate ghost cells (Voc 1.47--1.53~V, FF 91--92\%, up to 27\%). Practical flags that catch them: Voc above the $E_g$-implied ceiling for the modelled gap, or FF above Green's ideal-diode value at the measured Voc. All values in this paper are stated in the units the script layer expects; the archived logs record both.
